title: Drainage response transactional runtime owner closeout - architecture invariants 1-30
scope: Owner qualification of the F-PM14 drainage-response runtime composition and regression preservation of already admitted precomputed-DIVDRA and fixed-weir routes. This audit does not constitute independent F-VQ qualification or canonical admission.

invariants.evidence: F-PM14 extends the existing process/runtime composition and does not introduce a second SWAP kernel or use-case-specific executable.
mod_fmr_drainage_response_binding contains no file, path, parser, OPEN/READ/WRITE, .swp or calendar I/O assumptions; owner static guard passed.
Immutable drainage response parameters, interval control/forcing, committed physical state and diagnostics remain distinct types/roles.
Drainage response adds no persistent process state; restart owner test reports FPM14_RESTART_NO_ADDITIONAL_DRAINAGE_STATE=PASS.
Level exchanges and evaluation diagnostics are call-local/worker-side temporaries and are not stored as permanent column solver scratch.
MultiSWAP active/inactive/active isolation and execution-order independence passed at O0 and O2.
Active accepted trial commits once; unsupported response path rolls back with committed revision/state unchanged.
Restart continuation equivalence passed and no drainage-response hidden persistent state is required; retries remain based on committed transactional state.
Owner test uses non-calendar interval t0=9123.125, t1=9123.375; binding static guard rejects midnight/calendar assumptions.
F-PM14 does not specialize or constrain coupling-window duration or alignment.
Drainage response is composed through existing transactional runtime contracts; groundwater coupling machinery is neither bypassed nor forked.
The explicit SWAP-MODFLOW bottom-interface contract is outside the changed production set and is not altered by F-PM14.
Owner gate proves hard accepted mass closure, authoritative ledger ownership and exactly-once accepted drainage transfer; response binding itself does not double-book mass.
Drainage response diagnostics expose derivative_defined and dq_dgroundwater_level per level, while the separate bottom-interface sensitivity contract remains untouched.
F-PM14 introduces direct response evaluations inside the normal trial path and no structural extra full-SWAP coupling runs.
MultiSWAP isolation/order tests pass; no separate heavyweight solver instance or persistent response state is added per column.
MODFLOW cell/tile fraction composition is unchanged and remains outside the SWAP kernel.
Deep-vadose transfer-zone contracts and ownership are untouched.
No deep-vadose/direct-coupling transition storage or transfer accounting is modified.
Drainage response consumes process_hydraulic_view_t rather than a concrete Richards/HeadCalc internal representation.
Drainage physics is implemented as shared process modules and is composed through the common runtime rather than copied into a solver-specific path.
Owner static guard confirms the drainage-response binding has no HeadCalc-internal dependency.
Drainage response variants/configuration are physical configuration; no solver-performance policy silently changes those variants.
F-PM14 adds bounded direct process evaluations and no unbounded retry/fallback loop. No throughput-performance claim is made by this workunit.
Reference mode/reference solver authority is outside the changed production set and remains available.
Runtime exposes explicit active/rejected response diagnostics, per-level response data, evaluation counts and accepted mass-accounting evidence.
Inactive columns need no drainage-response persistent state; active/inactive/active MultiSWAP isolation passed.
System composition, tile relations and coupling ownership remain in runtime/coupler layers; F-PM14 does not move them into SWAP physics.
Static guards and generic-interval test exclude implicit .swp, path, midnight, day-length and direct-MODFLOW assumptions in the new binding.
This file records explicit invariant 1-30 disposition plus green owner and preservation gates on the exact tested candidate head.

preservation.precomputed_divdra: PASS - F-CI33 admitted oracle/source locks, valid publication, scalar mass preservation, B1.10 consumer seam, zero path, rejection, overwrite guard and O0/O2 exact output identity replayed on current postimage.
preservation.fixed_weir: PASS - F-PM08D7 admitted test sources are byte-locked; unchanged fixed-weir production authorities, process behavior, O0/O2 compilation, transaction/rollback, restart and temporal semantics were replayed on current postimage. Historical compile runners were augmented ephemerally only with the new backend module dependencies; assertions and test programs remained unchanged.
